messages:
envoy-bot: ALERT: hosted-inference /v1/generate 503 spike (region-us-east-1). 1200 errors in 5m, p95 latency 2.1s, p99 4.8s. auto-escalation to #incidents.
cs-alia: getting customer report — multiple requests time out, customer seeing 503s and getting charged for retries. Ping SRE oncall.
maria-oncall: on it. looking at topo, seems concentrated on pool infer-us-east-rtg-2. Any recent deploys?
alex: we had a small runtime deploy 11m ago that enabled dynbatch for streaming endpoints (flag: enable_stream_dynbatch=true). I can roll back if needed.
ben: adding logs: kubectl logs infer-runner-7f8c -n hosted --previous shows container exit code 137 then restart loop.
jordan-eng: stack shows CUDA OOM in attention kernel right before exit: 
```
E [2026-03-16T09:10:03Z] infer_runner: runtime error: CUDA out of memory when allocating 128MB for attn_kv_cache
E [2026-03-16T09:10:03Z] infer_runner: process killed (signal 9)
```

maria-oncall: 137 is OOM-kill. But we should confirm whether kernel OOM (OOM killer) or GPU OOM. Any dmesg from host?
alex: grabbing node dmesg and nvidia-smi logs now.
infra-bot: Retrieved node logs: 
- kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 19876 (infer_runner) total-vm:...
- nvidia-smi topo: GPU memory usage spike, GPU 0 went to 99%

alex: nvidia-smi shows multiple infer_runner processes allocating large KV caches during streaming requests with long contexts (60k tokens). Looks like dynbatch aggregated too many sequences and blew out GPU memory.
cs-alia: customer uses streaming with long contexts, they said they ramped up concurrency. They want ETA and whether we can credit retries.
maria-oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) disable dynbatch streaming flag in runtime config for that pool, 2) route traffic away from pool to fallback pool with smaller models, 3) increase eviction threshold / restart backoff to avoid rapid thrashing. Can someone run the rollback?
\jalex?: (typo) disregard
alex: I can flip the flag and push a config rollback to pool in ~3m. Also creating fallback route to model-small-1 (lower memory) for the affected customer.
ben: rolling flag back: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/infer-runtime -n hosted ENABLE_STREAM_DYNBATCH=false --record
kubectl rollout restart deploy/infer-runtime -n hosted
```
jordan-eng: dumping a reproduction script for QA: heavy-streaming-repro.sh that opens 200 concurrent streams of 30k tokens with small sleep between chunks. We'll run in staging first.

alex: rollback in progress, rollout status shows 80% updated, some old pods still terminating.
infra-bot: Observability: 60s after rollback start, error-rate down 40%. p95 latency back to 700ms.
maria-oncall: good. While that's stabilizing, we need postmortem info: root cause hypothesis is dynbatch over-aggregation + long streaming contexts causing KV cache growth beyond GPU limits. Secondary factor: a recent quantized runtime change reduced memory headroom slightly.
jordan-eng: noted a warning in the runtime build: "KV cache prefetch multiplier changed (0.9 -> 1.1)" in the deploy from 11m ago. Might have nudged memory usage up.
ben: collecting core dumps from the crashed pods (using gcore) and uploading to /mnt/triage/artifacts/7160001234/. Also grabbed infer_runner logs, gcov traces.

cs-alia: customer comms draft: "we identified a runtime configuration change that increased batching for streaming requests which, combined with long-context usage, caused upstream worker memory exhaustion and 503s. We've rolled back the change and applied a fallback routing. We're continuing analysis and will follow up with mitigation and credits." Thoughts?
maria-oncall: good start. Add ETA for follow-up PM (24h) and immediate mitigation done. Offer transient retries credit.
alex: QA repro successful in staging — dynbatch enabled leads to OOM with 150 concurrent streams of 30k tokens. Disabled prevents OOM at same concurrency.
jordan-eng: remediation plan: short-term: keep dynbatch disabled for streaming; roll back quant change; place limit on per-stream KV cache (circuit-breaker) and cap aggregate batch size. Medium-term: implement dynamic KV eviction policy & backpressure signals to API gateway.
ben: I'm opening a ticket to track follow-ups and billing impact: TKT-12891. tagging billing and customer-success.
cs-alia: thx. I'll patch customer note and request credits. Please attach logs and timing for billing window.
maria-oncall: checklist for postmortem: - timeline, - deploy diff, - reproducer, - mitigations, - long-term fixes, - monitoring rule to alert on sustained GPU mem >85% for >60s. Assigning owners: jordan -> reproducer + KV eviction design, alex -> runtime rollback validation + config gating, ben -> artifact collection + ticketing, cs-alia -> customer comms.
alex: assigned, will follow up in doc. :thumbsup:
cs-alia: customer updated. they acknowledged and asked for link to postmortem. I'll keep them in the loop. :eyes:
infra-bot: Incident annotated: severity=sev2, owner=maria-oncall, incident_id=INC-7160001234
end of thread
